context: PRD-004 originally scoped bowtie as a 3-item linked group built on the linked-group mechanism.
choice: Built bowtie as a self-contained aggregate type instead — a single slide with a fixed 5-slot ans/res array (condition + 2 sorted actions + 2 sorted monitors), reusing Evaluate.GAP/Result.CORRELATED unchanged.
rationale: Real NCLEX bowtie items are answered as one screen with all three parts visible and submitted together, not as sequential screens. Building it as a linked group would mean 3 separate screens, diverging from real exam presentation. The single-slide encoding needed no new evaluation strategy and no new SlideInterface answer-group fields.
alternatives: 3-item linked group rendered as sequential screens

context: The linked-group mechanism (case-study/trend cluster) needs to construct arbitrary child slide types generically. Doing this as a registered SlideType (the way vocab flattens to Mc) would require the new type's own file to import initSlide/getInstance from slideFactory.ts — the same file that must import the new type's factory to register it — a circular import.
choice: Implemented cluster expansion as a special case in jsonProcessor.ts's _initSlide2 (type: cluster is intercepted and expanded via item.set before ever reaching initSlide/getInstance), not as a registered SlideType.
rationale: jsonProcessor.ts already imports initSlide and sits outside the slidetype/types layer, so no cycle is introduced. yarn circular enforces zero circular dependencies project-wide as a hard requirement.
alternatives: Register Cluster as a SlideType with getSlideSet() calling initSlide() recursively (circular import)
Hardcode a small fixed set of importable child factories like Vocab does (loses generality — clusters need arbitrary child types)

context: Special-casing type: cluster only in jsonProcessor.ts left reviewExtractor.ts's BoundaryMapBuilder/PoolExtractor and scoreProcessor.ts's ScoreProcessor blind to cluster expansion, since all three call initSlide() directly on top-level YAML items. Since cluster isn't a registered SlideType, initSlide() silently fell back to treating it as a single info slide, undercounting lesson/unit/course boundaries by (childCount-1) per cluster and causing the review-boundary prompt to fire mid-cluster — caught by the full Cypress e2e run against review.cy.ts, not by unit tests alone.
choice: Added the same type === 'cluster' special case to BoundaryMapBuilder.exercises(), PoolExtractor.exercises(), and ScoreProcessor.exercises(), each iterating item.set directly and adding regression tests to reviewExtractor.test.ts.
rationale: Duplicates cluster-awareness across four call sites rather than one, but a shared registered-type approach was blocked by the circular-import constraint from the prior decision.
alternatives: Leave review/score paths uncorrected (rejected — real, reachable bug affecting the review boundary system and ProgressTable.vue's score summary)

context: Five new Vue exercise components (Bins, ClozeText, ClozeTable, MatrixSingle, MatrixMulti) initialized their state arrays inside onMounted() rather than synchronously, following the same onMounted-init pattern already used by GapExercise/SortExercise.
choice: Moved state initialization to run synchronously in <script setup> (immediately after the init() function definition) rather than deferring to onMounted(); onMounted() now only handles the restored-answer case.
rationale: The template's first render happens before onMounted fires. GapExercise/SortExercise are safe because their templates guard rendering on the not-yet-initialized array's length (e.g. v-if="j < slotLists.length"); the new components' templates lacked an equivalent guard and indexed directly into the still-empty state array, which crashed outright for MatrixMulti (.has() on undefined) and likely silently mis-rendered for the others. Found via the real Cypress e2e run, not unit tests.
alternatives: Add v-if guards matching Gap/Sort's pattern instead of restructuring initialization (rejected — synchronous init removes the footgun entirely rather than requiring every future new type to remember an equivalent guard)

context: Extended (partial-credit) multiple response needed a concrete scoring formula; PRD-004 flagged this as TBD against real NCLEX partial-credit rules, which aren't publicly specified in detail.
choice: Result.PARTIAL computes max(0, correctSelections - incorrectSelections) / totalCorrectAnswers, floored at 0.
rationale: A common, defensible 0..1 partial-credit scheme for select-N items: full credit only for an exact match, proportional credit for partial matches, no negative score for over-selecting.
alternatives: 0/1 credit per option against the full option pool (would need the option pool, not just ans/res, available at the Result-strategy call site)
All-or-nothing scoring (defeats the purpose of building extended SATA at all)
